protocol: Exact historical user prompts in fresh visible Colibri conversations, original followups in same conversation. One attempt per prompt; no teaching or feedback before completion. Five responses across three cases. Expectations frozen before sending. Historical Lucy comparison, not matched system prompts or current Lucy rerun.
grading: Practical correctness and usefulness separate from precision/style. Harmless terminology observations alone do not fail. Fail material contradictions or misleading advice. Do not require extra facts not requested.

settings.effective_reasoning: Flint may reason despite UI checkbox off

prompts: An insulated picnic cooler contains ice at 0 C in a 30 C room. It has no powered refrigeration. Explain in two short sentences what the insulation does and whether it can prevent the ice from melting indefinitely. Do not use tools.
cases.expected: Insulation reduces incoming heat and slows melting; finite insulation does not prevent melting indefinitely.

prompts: GPU activity diagnostic 2: Explain how insulation slows heat transfer, using general physical principles in about 250 words. This is a hardware timing check. Do not use tools.
Summarize your previous explanation in one short sentence.
cases.earlier: Oct 31 f16 final check said insulation keeps hot components cooler; repeated in summary.
criteria: Explain reduced heat transfer, not active cooling or universal cooling of hot components.
Summary preserves direction and does not add unsupported cooling claims.

prompts: This is a hypothetical troubleshooting exercise. Use the supplied facts; do not inspect or change the real Phoenix system. My photo storage has two disks in a mirror. Every night, another drive is synchronized to it, including deletions; it has no version history. I also have a disconnected backup made last Friday. On Monday I accidentally deleted a family album, and the nightly sync has already copied that deletion. Are the mirror and synchronized drive enough to recover the deleted album? What should I try next, without putting the surviving photos at risk?

I checked: Friday's disconnected backup does contain the family album. A new folder of Saturday photos is absent from that backup and is also now missing from both current drives. Should I restore the entire Friday backup over the live storage? Tell me what we can recover with confidence and what we cannot promise.

criteria.prompt: This is a hypothetical troubleshooting exercise. Use the supplied facts; do not inspect or change the real Phoenix system. My photo storage has two disks in a mirror. Every night, another drive is synchronized to it, including deletions; it has no version history. I also have a disconnected backup made last Friday. On Monday I accidentally deleted a family album, and the nightly sync has already copied that deletion. Are the mirror and synchronized drive enough to recover the deleted album? What should I try next, without putting the surviving photos at risk?
criteria.pass: Mirror/sync do not guarantee recovery from replicated deletion; inspect Friday offline backup and recover album if present; protect surviving data, avoid syncing deletion to only backup or destructive full restore. Optional undelete/trash/snapshots conditional, not invented.
criteria.material_fail: Says mirror or sync necessarily retains deletion history; guarantees undelete; destructive whole-disk restore or sync over only good backup.

criteria.prompt: I checked: Friday's disconnected backup does contain the family album. A new folder of Saturday photos is absent from that backup and is also now missing from both current drives. Should I restore the entire Friday backup over the live storage? Tell me what we can recover with confidence and what we cannot promise.
criteria.pass: Recover known album from verified backup with targeted restore/alternate folder and verify; do not overwrite whole live storage needlessly. Saturday photos cannot be promised; investigate other sources/trash/recovery cautiously; do not claim definitely impossible.
criteria.material_fail: Claims Friday copy contains later Saturday data; promises recovery without source; directs destructive full restore over surviving newer data.

limitations: Small failure-selected sample is not everyday accuracy.
Lucy uses Heretic GPT-OSS20B with production prompt/memory; Flint uses Colibri without those tools or memory.
Cooler and insulation errors repeated historically; photo-recovery failure documented once, not established recurring.
No Lucy production settings or memories will change.
